body_markdown:
Honda is investing hefty sums to expand its presence in the American market. The latest announcements from the brand include[a new, $3 billion factory in Ohio](https://hondanews.com/en-US/honda-corporate/releases/release-b26ae02ff5dca50cb32a1f4783115123-honda-to-boost-us-hybrid-production-with-new-3-billion-us-auto-plant-and-investments-in-multiple-facilities) to make hybrid models, and it has confirmed that the next-generation CR-V due out for 2028 will be only available with hybrid power. And, most interestingly for lovers of quirky, boxy, practical conveyances, unverified reports claim that a new Element will join the next Honda CR-V in showrooms by 2029.


Dealers who attended a closed-door meeting in Las Vegas, Nevada, on November 11 told *Automotive News* that[the long-awaited next-gen Element](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/the-elements-of-a-new-honda-element-must-be-rooted-in-the-original/) that has been rumored for years is now on its way to production.


The anonymous sources who spoke with the publication sketched the outline of a subcompact crossover positioned between the HR-V and the CR-V. Like the original Element, which was sold from 2003 to 2011, the next-generation model will be aimed at young, urban buyers who want a relatively affordable car that’s equally at home in the city and in the backcountry. The model shown during the meeting featured a boxy silhouette and the rear-hinged rear doors that helped the original Element stand out in a crowded segment. Hybrid power will be available, and production is reportedly scheduled to start in the second quarter of 2029.

Honda


The CR-V is Honda’s bread-and-butter model: It’s the company’s best-selling car in the United States, which is its largest and most profitable market. To win over even more buyers, Honda improved fuel efficiency by over 10% compared to[the outgoing CR-V](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/hondas-sixth-gen-cr-v-gains-more-hybrid-power-classier-style-for-2023/) while improving performance. The brand hasn’t released specific figures, but it said power will come from a new, two-motor hybrid system built around an Atkinson-cycle four-cylinder engine. Front-wheel-drive will likely continue to come standard, and what the brand calls a “newly developed electric AWD unit” will be available on some trim levels. While this is pure speculation, it sounds a lot like a through-the-road system, with the engine driving the front wheels and electric motors powering the rear wheels.


Honda


Honda’s preview image leaves a lot to the imagination: It only shows a redesigned “CR-V” emblem. However, anonymous insiders who claim they recently got a preview of the next-gen CR-V told[Automotive News](https://www.autonews.com/honda/an-honda-reveals-product-roadmap-at-dealer-meeting-1112/) that it’s characterized by a boxier, more upright front end with thin headlights and a more muscular-looking rear end with a full-width light bar. There’s more tech inside, including a 15.4-inch touchscreen for some trim levels. The updated styling hides a new, modular platform that will underpin other models.


Due out as a 2028 model, the next Honda CR-V will be manufactured in Ohio, in Indiana, and in Canada. Honda will build the model in three factories because it has high expectations for it: Insiders told *Automotive News* that executives plan to sell more than 400,000 units of the next CR-V during the first full year of production. There’s no word yet on when we’ll see it, but the 2028 label hints at an unveiling during the first half of 2027. That’s good timing: The CR-V nameplate will turn 30 years old in 2027.


Honda added that the seventh-generation CR-V is the first of several hybrid models it will launch in the United States by 2030. It hasn’t detailed the other cars in the pipeline.


Beyond the CR-V and the Element, Honda is also working on a more upscale[Accord](https://www.hagerty.com/media/automotive-history/honda-accord-50-years-of-quiet-competence/) and a more rugged-looking[Ridgeline](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/honda-improves-2024-ridgeline-with-trailsport-trim-tech-updates/) . The hotter Civic Type R[previewed at SEMA 2026](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/honda-civic-type-r-hrc-sema-2026/) is around the corner as well, and it’s being developed by Honda’s race car engineers.


The post[Honda Element Reboot Rumors Persist, CR-V Going Hybrid-Only](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/2028-honda-cr-v-hybrid-launch-date-element-rumors/) appeared first on[Hagerty Media](https://www.hagerty.com/media) .
